name: Learn 10–15 useful knots
blurb: A well-chosen dozen covers a lifetime: a loop, a hitch, a bend, a friction knot and a couple of specialists. The skill is in choosing the right one and tying it under pressure.
gear: Two lengths of 6–8 mm rope, different colours, about two metres each
A rail or post to tie to
steps: Loops: bowline, figure-eight on a bight, alpine butterfly.
Hitches: clove hitch, two half hitches, taut-line hitch, timber hitch, trucker’s hitch for tensioning.
Bends for joining ropes: sheet bend (works with unequal thicknesses), double fisherman’s.
Stoppers and specials: figure-eight stopper, prusik, constrictor, and a quick-release highwayman’s hitch.
Learn each one in three passes: watch, tie slowly ten times, then tie it while talking about something else.
Use them for real — guy lines, roof racks, washing lines — because context is what makes them stick.
tips: Learn what each knot is for and how it fails, not just the shape. A bowline is not a climbing anchor by itself.
Dress and set every knot: neat, no crossed strands, tightened evenly.
A knot you can only tie in one orientation is not learned yet.
proof: You tie all fifteen from memory in under five minutes, and pick the right knot for three real tasks.
